subproblems.title: Linear lower bound for a C¹ map near a point where its derivative is injective
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝᵐ be open, let φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N be C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 φ V), let v₀ ∈ V, and suppose that Dφ(v₀) := fderiv ℝ φ v₀ is injective. Then there exist c > 0 and δ > 0 such that the closed ball B_δ(v₀) is contained in V and c‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)‖ for every w ∈ ℝᵐ with ‖w‖ ≤ δ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn m)) (φ : Rn m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (v₀ : Rn m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 φ V → v₀ ∈ V → Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ φ v₀) → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ closedBall v₀ δ ⊆ V ∧ ∀ w : Rn m, ‖w‖ ≤ δ → c * ‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ (v₀ + w) - φ v₀‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only): step 2 of the parent proof (the lower bound (a)); the proof below is self-contained.
Notation: B_ρ(p) is the closed ball and B̆_ρ(p) the open ball; L := Dφ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ φ v₀.
1. Antilipschitz bound for L. L is a linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ with trivial kernel (it is injective; LinearMap.ker_eq_bot). By LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith there is K > 0 such that L is K-antilipschitz; AntilipschitzWith.le_mul_dist applied to u and 0 gives ‖u‖ ≤ K‖Lu‖ for every u ∈ ℝᵐ. Put c := 1/(2K) > 0. Then 2c‖u‖ = ‖u‖/K ≤ ‖Lu‖ for every u.
2. Choice of δ. Since V is open and φ is C¹ on V, v ↦ Dφ(v) is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, 1 ≤ 1), hence continuous at v₀ ∈ V. Choose δ₁ > 0 with ‖Dφ(v) − L‖ < c whenever dist(v, v₀) < δ₁ (Metric.continuousAt_iff) and δ₂ > 0 with B̆_{δ₂}(v₀) ⊆ V (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂)/2 > 0. Then δ < δ₁ and δ < δ₂, so B_δ(v₀) ⊆ B̆_{δ₂}(v₀) ⊆ V (closedBall_subset_ball). This is the first assertion.
3. Differentiability on B_δ(v₀). φ is differentiable on V (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn, since the order 1 is nonzero). Every v ∈ B_δ(v₀) lies in the open set V, so φ is differentiable at v and has Fréchet derivative Dφ(v) there (DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt, DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt). Let g(v) := φ(v) − L(v − v₀). The map v ↦ L(v − v₀) has derivative L at every point (chain rule for the continuous linear map L after v ↦ v − v₀), so g has derivative Dφ(v) − L at every v ∈ B_δ(v₀) (HasFDerivAt.sub). For such v, dist(v, v₀) ≤ δ < δ₁, hence ‖fderiv ℝ g v‖ = ‖Dφ(v) − L‖ ≤ c.
4. Mean value inequality. Let w ∈ ℝᵐ with ‖w‖ ≤ δ. Then v₀ ∈ B_δ(v₀) and v₀ + w ∈ B_δ(v₀). The closed ball B_δ(v₀) is convex, so Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le, applied to g on B_δ(v₀) with the bound c of step 3, gives ‖g(v₀ + w) − g(v₀)‖ ≤ c‖(v₀ + w) − v₀‖ = c‖w‖. Since g(v₀ + w) − g(v₀) = φ(v₀ + w) − Lw − φ(v₀), this reads ‖φ(v₀ + w) − Lw − φ(v₀)‖ ≤ c‖w‖.
5. Conclusion. Since Lw = (φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)) − (φ(v₀ + w) − Lw − φ(v₀)), the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 4 give 2c‖w‖ ≤ ‖Lw‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)‖ + ‖φ(v₀ + w) − Lw − φ(v₀)‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)‖ + c‖w‖. Hence c‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)‖ for every w with ‖w‖ ≤ δ.
proof_key_steps: L := Dφ(v₀) is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝᵐ, so ‖u‖ ≤ K‖Lu‖ for some K > 0; put c := 1/(2K)
continuity of Dφ at v₀ and openness of V give δ > 0 with B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V and ‖Dφ(v) − L‖ ≤ c on B_δ(v₀)
mean value inequality for g(v) = φ(v) − L(v − v₀) on the convex ball B_δ(v₀): ‖φ(v₀+w) − φ(v₀) − Lw‖ ≤ c‖w‖
triangle inequality with ‖Lw‖ ≥ 2c‖w‖ gives c‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀+w) − φ(v₀)‖

subproblems.title: Separation of remote chart parameters by properness and injectivity
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝᵐ be an arbitrary set, let W ⊆ ℝ^N be an open set, and let φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N be continuous on V and injective on V. Let v₀ ∈ V with φ(v₀) ∈ W, and assume that V ∩ φ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every δ > 0 there is ε > 0 such that ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ for every v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn m)) (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))) (φ : Rn m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (v₀ : Rn m), IsOpen W → ContinuousOn φ V → InjOn φ V → v₀ ∈ V → φ v₀ ∈ W → (∀ K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → IsCompact (V ∩ φ ⁻¹' K)) → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ v ∈ V, δ ≤ ‖v - v₀‖ → ε ≤ ‖φ v - φ v₀‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only): step 3 of the parent proof (separation (b)), with Q written as (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∩ {δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖} = (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∖ B̆_δ(v₀) and ε₀ chosen so that B_{ε₀}(x) ⊆ W; only continuity of φ on V, injectivity of φ on V and the properness hypothesis are used, and V need not be open.
Notation: x := φ(v₀); B_ρ(p) is the closed ball and B̆_ρ(p) the open ball. Fix δ > 0.
1. Choice of ε₀. W is open and x ∈ W, so there is ε₁ > 0 with B̆_{ε₁}(x) ⊆ W (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put ε₀ := ε₁/2 > 0. Then K₀ := B_{ε₀}(x) ⊆ B̆_{ε₁}(x) ⊆ W (closedBall_subset_ball), and K₀ is compact (isCompact_closedBall; ℝ^N is proper).
2. The compact set Q. By the properness hypothesis applied to K₀, the set V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀) is compact. The set D := {v ∈ ℝᵐ : δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖} is closed (isClosed_le of two continuous functions). Hence Q := (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∩ D is compact (IsCompact.inter_right). Since Q ⊆ V and φ is continuous on V, the function v ↦ ‖φ(v) − x‖ is continuous on Q.
3. Case Q ≠ ∅. A continuous function on a nonempty compact set attains its minimum (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn): there is q ∈ Q with ‖φ(q) − x‖ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖ for every v ∈ Q. Moreover ‖φ(q) − x‖ > 0: otherwise φ(q) = φ(v₀) with q ∈ V and v₀ ∈ V, so q = v₀ by injectivity of φ on V, and then δ ≤ ‖q − v₀‖ = 0 contradicts δ > 0. Put ε := min(ε₀, ‖φ(q) − x‖) > 0. Let v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖. If φ(v) ∈ K₀, then v ∈ Q, so ε ≤ ‖φ(q) − x‖ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖. If φ(v) ∉ K₀, then ‖φ(v) − x‖ > ε₀ ≥ ε.
4. Case Q = ∅. Put ε := ε₀ > 0. Let v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖. If ‖φ(v) − x‖ < ε₀, then φ(v) ∈ K₀, so v ∈ Q, which is impossible. Hence ε = ε₀ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖.
5. In both cases ε > 0 and ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ for every v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖.
proof_key_steps: a closed ball K₀ = B_{ε₀}(φ(v₀)) ⊆ W, compact
Q = (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∩ {v : δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖} is compact by properness
the minimum of ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ on Q (if Q ≠ ∅) is positive by injectivity on V
ε := min(ε₀, that minimum), or ε₀ if Q = ∅; points with φ(v) ∉ K₀ are farther than ε₀

subproblems.title: The rescaled chart is an injective parametrization of the blow-up with the same derivative
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝᵐ open, φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N differentiable on V and injective on V, v₀ ∈ ℝᵐ and r ∈ ℝ with r ≠ 0. Put U_r := {u ∈ ℝᵐ : v₀ + ru ∈ V} and ψ_r(u) := r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)). Then (i) U_r is open; (ii) ψ_r is injective on U_r; (iii) ψ_r(U_r) = η_{φ(v₀),r}(φ(V)), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) is Chapter03.blowUpMap x r; (iv) for every u ∈ U_r, ψ_r has Fréchet derivative fderiv ℝ φ (v₀ + ru) at u (HasFDerivAt).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn m)) (φ : Rn m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (v₀ : Rn m) (r : ℝ), IsOpen V → DifferentiableOn ℝ φ V → InjOn φ V → r ≠ 0 → IsOpen {u : Rn m | v₀ + r • u ∈ V} ∧ InjOn (fun u : Rn m => r⁻¹ • (φ (v₀ + r • u) - φ v₀)) {u : Rn m | v₀ + r • u ∈ V} ∧ (fun u : Rn m => r⁻¹ • (φ (v₀ + r • u) - φ v₀)) '' {u : Rn m | v₀ + r • u ∈ V} = Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap (φ v₀) r '' (φ '' V) ∧ ∀ u ∈ {u : Rn m | v₀ + r • u ∈ V}, HasFDerivAt (fun u : Rn m => r⁻¹ • (φ (v₀ + r • u) - φ v₀)) (fderiv ℝ φ (v₀ + r • u)) u
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only): step 4 of the parent proof: ψ_r is injective on U_r because φ is injective on V, u ↦ v₀ + ru is a bijection of U_r onto V so ψ_r(U_r) = η_{x,r}(φ(V)), and by the chain rule Dψ_r(u) = r⁻¹·Dφ(v₀ + ru)·r = Dφ(v₀ + ru). Here it is proved for any r ≠ 0 and any v₀.
Notation: U_r := {u : v₀ + ru ∈ V}, ψ_r(u) := r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)), η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x).
1. U_r is open: the map u ↦ v₀ + ru is continuous, and U_r is the preimage of the open set V under it (IsOpen.preimage).
2. ψ_r is injective on U_r. Let u₁, u₂ ∈ U_r with ψ_r(u₁) = ψ_r(u₂). Multiplying both sides by r and using r·r⁻¹ = 1 gives φ(v₀ + ru₁) − φ(v₀) = φ(v₀ + ru₂) − φ(v₀), so φ(v₀ + ru₁) = φ(v₀ + ru₂). Both v₀ + ru₁ and v₀ + ru₂ lie in V and φ is injective on V, so v₀ + ru₁ = v₀ + ru₂. Cancelling v₀ gives ru₁ = ru₂, and since r ≠ 0, u₁ = u₂.
3. ψ_r(U_r) ⊆ η_{φ(v₀),r}(φ(V)). For u ∈ U_r put v := v₀ + ru ∈ V. Then ψ_r(u) = r⁻¹(φ(v) − φ(v₀)) = η_{φ(v₀),r}(φ(v)) with φ(v) ∈ φ(V).
4. η_{φ(v₀),r}(φ(V)) ⊆ ψ_r(U_r). Let v ∈ V and put u := r⁻¹(v − v₀). Then v₀ + ru = v₀ + (r·r⁻¹)(v − v₀) = v ∈ V, so u ∈ U_r, and ψ_r(u) = r⁻¹(φ(v) − φ(v₀)) = η_{φ(v₀),r}(φ(v)). With step 3 this proves (iii).
5. Derivative. Fix u ∈ U_r and put v := v₀ + ru ∈ V. Since V is open and φ is differentiable on V, φ is differentiable at v, so φ has Fréchet derivative Dφ(v) := fderiv ℝ φ v at v. The affine map u ↦ v₀ + ru has derivative r·id (derivative of the identity scaled by r, plus a constant). By the chain rule, u ↦ φ(v₀ + ru) has derivative Dφ(v) ∘ (r·id) at u; subtracting the constant φ(v₀) leaves it unchanged, and multiplying by the constant r⁻¹ shows that ψ_r has derivative r⁻¹·(Dφ(v) ∘ (r·id)) at u. For every w ∈ ℝᵐ, linearity gives r⁻¹·Dφ(v)(rw) = (r⁻¹·r)·Dφ(v)(w) = Dφ(v)(w), so this continuous linear map equals Dφ(v) (ext; HasFDerivAt.congr_fderiv). Hence ψ_r has Fréchet derivative fderiv ℝ φ (v₀ + ru) at u.
proof_key_steps: U_r is the preimage of the open set V under the continuous map u ↦ v₀ + ru
injectivity of ψ_r on U_r from injectivity of φ on V and r ≠ 0
u ↦ v₀ + ru maps U_r onto V, giving ψ_r(U_r) = η_{φ(v₀),r}(φ(V))
chain rule: Dψ_r(u) = r⁻¹·(Dφ(v₀+ru) ∘ r·id) = Dφ(v₀+ru)

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for the rescaled chart integrals
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝᵐ open, φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N continuous on V, J : ℝᵐ → ℝ continuous on V, L : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N a continuous linear map and v₀ ∈ ℝᵐ such that φ has Fréchet derivative L at v₀. Let c, δ, ε > 0 with B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V (closed ball) such that (a) c‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)‖ for every w with ‖w‖ ≤ δ, and (b) ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ for every v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖. Let f : ℝ^N → ℝ be continuous with compact support. With Hᵐ := μHE[m] on ℝᵐ, U_r := {u ∈ ℝᵐ : v₀ + ru ∈ V} and ψ_r(u) := r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)), we have ∫_{U_r} J(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)) dHᵐ(u) → ∫_{ℝᵐ} J(v₀)·f(Lu) dHᵐ(u) as r → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn m)) (φ : Rn m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (J : Rn m → ℝ) (L : Rn m →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (v₀ : Rn m) (c δ ε : ℝ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) → ℝ), IsOpen V → ContinuousOn φ V → ContinuousOn J V → HasFDerivAt φ L v₀ → 0 < c → 0 < δ → 0 < ε → closedBall v₀ δ ⊆ V → (∀ w : Rn m, ‖w‖ ≤ δ → c * ‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ (v₀ + w) - φ v₀‖) → (∀ v ∈ V, δ ≤ ‖v - v₀‖ → ε ≤ ‖φ v - φ v₀‖) → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ u in {u : Rn m | v₀ + r • u ∈ V}, J (v₀ + r • u) * f (r⁻¹ • (φ (v₀ + r • u) - φ v₀)) ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Rn m))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ u, J v₀ * f (L u) ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Rn m))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only): steps 5, 6 and 7 (dominated convergence) of the parent proof, with J_φ replaced by an arbitrary function J continuous on V; the constants R, M and Λ are constructed below and (a), (b) are hypotheses, so the proof is self-contained.
Notation: g_r(u) := J(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)), F_r := 1_{U_r}·g_r; B_ρ(p) is the closed ball.
1. Measure and base point. On ℝᵐ, Hᵐ = μHE[m] equals Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so we work with Lebesgue measure, which is finite on compact sets. Since δ > 0, v₀ ∈ B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V.
2. Constants. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) for some R₀; put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. Then f(y) ≠ 0 implies ‖y‖ ≤ R. Since f is continuous with compact support, there is M with |f(y)| ≤ M for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). J is continuous on the compact set B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V, so there is Λ with |J(v)| ≤ Λ for v ∈ B_δ(v₀) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Also M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0 and Λ ≥ |J(v₀)| ≥ 0.
3. Indicator form. For every r, U_r is open (preimage of the open set V under the continuous map u ↦ v₀ + ru), hence measurable, and ∫_{U_r} g_r = ∫_{ℝᵐ} F_r (integral_indicator). So it suffices to prove ∫ F_r → ∫ J(v₀)·f(Lu) du as r → 0⁺.
4. Measurability. For every r, g_r is continuous on U_r: u ↦ v₀ + ru is continuous and maps U_r into V, J and φ are continuous on V (ContinuousOn.comp), u ↦ r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)) is then continuous on U_r, f is continuous, and products of continuous functions are continuous. Hence g_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to U_r (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable, U_r measurable), so F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff). No measurability of g_r off U_r is needed.
5. Domination. Let G := Λ·M·1_{B_{R/c}(0)}. G is integrable: it is a constant on the closed ball B_{R/c}(0), which has finite measure (integrableOn_const, IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator). Let 0 < r < ε/R, so rR < ε; this set of r belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). We show |F_r(u)| ≤ G(u) for every u. If u ∉ U_r or f(ψ_r(u)) = 0, then F_r(u) = 0 ≤ G(u) because G ≥ 0. Otherwise v := v₀ + ru ∈ V and ‖ψ_r(u)‖ ≤ R. As r > 0, ‖ψ_r(u)‖ = r⁻¹‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖, so ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ ≤ rR < ε. If δ ≤ ‖ru‖ = ‖v − v₀‖, hypothesis (b) would give ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖, a contradiction; hence ‖ru‖ < δ. Hypothesis (a) with w := ru gives c‖ru‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)‖ ≤ rR. Since ‖ru‖ = r‖u‖, this is r·(c‖u‖) ≤ r·R, so c‖u‖ ≤ R and ‖u‖ ≤ R/c, i.e. u ∈ B_{R/c}(0) and G(u) = ΛM. Also dist(v₀ + ru, v₀) = ‖ru‖ < δ, so |J(v₀ + ru)| ≤ Λ, and |f(ψ_r(u))| ≤ M. Therefore |F_r(u)| = |J(v₀ + ru)|·|f(ψ_r(u))| ≤ ΛM = G(u).
6. Pointwise limit. Fix u ∈ ℝᵐ. The map r ↦ v₀ + ru is continuous with value v₀ at r = 0, so v₀ + ru → v₀ as r → 0⁺. V is a neighbourhood of v₀, so eventually v₀ + ru ∈ V, i.e. u ∈ U_r and F_r(u) = g_r(u). J is continuous at v₀ (continuous on the open set V ∋ v₀), so J(v₀ + ru) → J(v₀). Next, ‖r⁻¹‖ → ∞ as r → 0⁺ (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero composed with the norm), so HasFDerivAt.lim with the scalars r⁻¹ gives r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + (r⁻¹)⁻¹u) − φ(v₀)) → Lu; since (r⁻¹)⁻¹ = r this says ψ_r(u) → Lu. As f is continuous, f(ψ_r(u)) → f(Lu), so g_r(u) → J(v₀)·f(Lu), and because F_r(u) = g_r(u) eventually, F_r(u) → J(v₀)·f(Lu) (Tendsto.congr').
7. Conclusion. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is countably generated. Dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence with the bound G and steps 4–6) gives ∫ F_r → ∫ J(v₀)·f(Lu) du as r → 0⁺. By step 3 and step 1 this is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Hᵐ = Lebesgue measure on ℝᵐ; constants R (support radius), M = sup|f|, Λ = sup of |J| on B_δ(v₀)
∫_{U_r} g_r = ∫ 1_{U_r} g_r with U_r open; F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable since g_r is continuous on U_r
for 0 < r < ε/R: if F_r(u) ≠ 0 then (b) forces ‖ru‖ < δ and (a) gives ‖u‖ ≤ R/c, so |F_r| ≤ ΛM·1_{B_{R/c}(0)}
pointwise: u ∈ U_r eventually, J(v₀+ru) → J(v₀), ψ_r(u) → Lu by HasFDerivAt.lim, so F_r(u) → J(v₀)f(Lu)
dominated convergence along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent spaces depend only on the set near the point
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, S, T ⊆ ℝ^N, x ∈ ℝ^N, ε > 0 and let P be a linear subspace of ℝ^N. Suppose S ∩ B̆_ε(x) = T ∩ B̆_ε(x) (open ball). If P is the approximate tangent space of T at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 with Hᵐ := μHE[m] (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m T x P), then P is the approximate tangent space of S at x (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m S x P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (S T : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (ε : ℝ) (P : Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))), 0 < ε → S ∩ ball x ε = T ∩ ball x ε → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m T x P → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m S x P
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only): step 4 of the parent proof, first half: since f vanishes off B := B_R(0), ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f = ∫_{η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B} f, and for rR < ε the sets η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B and η_{x,r}(W ∩ S) ∩ B coincide. Here it is stated for any two sets that agree near x.
Notation: η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x); B_ρ(p) closed ball, B̆_ρ(p) open ball; all integrals are with respect to Hᵐ = μHE[m] on ℝ^N.
1. Dimension. finrank P = m is the first component of the hypothesis for T.
2. Support radius. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ). tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) for some R₀. Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0 and B := B_R(0). Then f(y) = 0 for y ∉ B.
3. Cutting off. For every set A ⊆ ℝ^N, ∫_A f = ∫_{A ∩ B} f. Indeed f = 1_B·f pointwise by step 2, and setIntegral_indicator gives ∫_A 1_B f = ∫_{A ∩ B} f; it only needs B measurable (B is closed). No measurability of A is needed.
4. The cut-off blow-ups agree. Let 0 < r < ε/R, so rR < ε. First, if A ∩ B̆_ε(x) ⊆ A′, then η_{x,r}(A) ∩ B ⊆ η_{x,r}(A′) ∩ B. Indeed, let y = r⁻¹(z − x) with z ∈ A and ‖y‖ ≤ R. Since r > 0, ‖y‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖, so ‖z − x‖ ≤ rR < ε. Thus z ∈ A ∩ B̆_ε(x) ⊆ A′ and y ∈ η_{x,r}(A′). Apply this with (A, A′) = (T, S), using T ∩ B̆_ε(x) = S ∩ B̆_ε(x) ⊆ S, and with (A, A′) = (S, T), using S ∩ B̆_ε(x) = T ∩ B̆_ε(x) ⊆ T. Hence η_{x,r}(T) ∩ B = η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B.
5. Conclusion. For 0 < r < ε/R, steps 3 and 4 give ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f = ∫_{η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B} f = ∫_{η_{x,r}(T) ∩ B} f = ∫_{η_{x,r}(T)} f. The interval (0, ε/R) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), so the two functions of r agree eventually as r → 0⁺. By hypothesis, ∫_{η_{x,r}(T)} f → ∫_P f as r → 0⁺; hence ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f → ∫_P f as well (Tendsto.congr'). Since f was arbitrary and finrank P = m, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m S x P holds.
proof_key_steps: finrank P = m is inherited from T
f vanishes off B = B_R(0), so ∫_A f = ∫_{A ∩ B} f for every A (setIntegral_indicator)
for 0 < r < ε/R, η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B = η_{x,r}(T) ∩ B because S and T agree on B̆_ε(x)
the blow-up integrals of S and T agree eventually as r → 0⁺, so the limit transfers
